resources.string: Drag the lower area sideways or tap a dot. The heading above is a second pager that follows it.
The page leaves under the finger while its neighbour follows it in.
Let go after %1$d%% of the width, or with a quick flick, and it lands on the neighbour. Anything less glides back.
A page is created the first time it is needed, and only once.
The first and the last page stop at the edge and do not over-scroll.
The buttons move the pager above. The heading and the dots follow as they do for a drag.
Page %1$d of %2$d, set without a glide
Off disables the pager: drags, keys and dots no longer move it, code still does.

Extracted from the original app: the first-launch flow with its page dots and its heading that moves in step with the content. New in Mallet: dots that blend, moving it from code, and the link as a public call.
